title: Histological quantification of cerebral cavernous malformations in the murine brain
protocol: Inject intraperitoneally the mouse with 0.4–0.75 mg/kg of Avertin.
Pinch the toe to ensure the mouse is deeply anesthetized.
Arrange the mouse on its back and pin the four limbs down.
Use forceps and scissors to clamp and cut the skin to expose the chest cavity.
Make an incision parallel and over the diaphragm to avoid piercing the lung and heart.
Uncover the heart by cutting laterally the ribs with the scissors.
Insert the perfusion needle in the apex of the left ventricle.
Cut open the right atrium with a small cut using scissors.
Perfuse the mouse with a peristaltic pump.
Perfuse initially with 5 mL PBS at room temperature to wash out blood.
Switch to 4% PFA and continue perfusion up to final volume.
Dissect the brain after stopping the pump.
Cut the head and uncover the skull by removing skin.
Open the skull using scissors under the lambda, cutting the sagittal and interfrontal suture.
Remove the brain from the skull with fine forceps.
Collect the brain in a 50 mL tube with at least 10 mL 4% PFA.
Post-fix the brain in at least 10 mL 4% PFA overnight at 4°C.
Wash the brain twice with PBS and leave it in PBS.
Remove internal organs to access the vertebral column if analyzing spinal cord.
Cut ribs and pelvis to remove the vertebral column from the animal.
Clean the vertebral column from skin and other tissues.
Collect the vertebral column in a 50 mL tube with at least 10 mL 4% PFA.
Post-fix the vertebral column in at least 10 mL 4% PFA overnight at 4°C.
Wash the vertebral column twice with PBS.
Perform ventral rostral-to-caudal laminectomy to gain access to the spinal cord.
Cut a 200 μL pipette tip to make a 2-3 mm hole and mount it on a 5 mL syringe.
Carefully flush out the spinal cord in a rostral-to-caudal direction into a 50 mL tube with PBS.
Dry the brain by rolling it over a paper towel.
Divide the cerebral hemispheres cutting the medial part with a blade.
Put one hemisphere in a disposable base mold (15 × 15 × 6 mm) with the inner face towards the bottom.
Cover the tissue with warm 4% low melting agarose solution and cool it on ice or at RT.
Transfer the solidified agarose block to the platform of the vibratome and fix it with glue.
Cut the whole cerebral hemisphere into 100 μm thick sagittal sections, at speed 1–1.5 mm/s and amplitude 1 mm.
Collect the sections in PBS.
Put 4/5 sections in each well of a 12-well plate keeping the order of sectioning.
Store sections either in PBS at 4°C for 2 or 3 days or for almost 1 month at −20°C in freezing solution (40% PBS, 30% Glycerol, 30% Ethylene glycol).
Select one section from each well in the 12-well plate and place them in a new well.
Incubate the selected sections in 1 mL blocking solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Incubate the sections with primary antibody anti-PECAM1, diluted 1:200 in fresh blocking solution (0.5 mL), overnight at 4°C.
Wash the sections three times with 1 mL PBS at room temperature for 10 minutes each.
Incubate the sections with goat anti-Hamster-CY3, diluted 1:200 in PBS, for 4 hours at room temperature.
Remove the solution and wash the sections three times with 1 mL PBS for 10 minutes each.
Post-fix the stained sections with 4% PFA for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the sections three times with 1 mL PBS for 10 minutes each.
Move brain sections into a petri dish filled with PBS-T (PBS + 0.01% Triton-X100).
Using a fine brush, mount the sections on a superfrost glass slide.
Let the mounted sections dry at room temperature for 20 minutes before mounting them with Vectashield solution.
Seal the slides with nail polish and leave overnight at 4°C.
Switch on the software and the laser.
Scan the whole slide with a 2.5× objective using the navigator system to visualize all brain sections.
Define a region of interest (ROI) around each single section.
Set the 10× objective and redefine the Z-stack of each section using a 10 μm z-step.
Acquire zoom 1×, bidirectional scanning with resolution set at 1024 × 1024 pixels and frequency 400 Hz.
Merge Z-stack images and save them as ".lif” files.
Open the Fiji software.
Open "set measurement" and select “Area”.
Perform Z-projection of the section with max intensity.
Calibrate the image to ensure dimensions are expressed in μm.
If not calibrated, refer to troubleshooting to calibrate the image.
Open the ROI MANAGER tool.
Draw the outline of the entire brain section and add it to the ROI Manager.
Draw the outline of each individual lesion and add it to the ROI Manager.
Measure the area of all ROIs using the “Measure all” tool of the ROI MANAGER.
Copy and paste the measurements from the “Results” window to an Excel file.
Convert the “Analyzed area” from μm² to mm² in cells D5:D7 of the Excel table.
Obtain the “Lesioned area” by summing the area of all lesions in cells F5:F7.
Count the number of lesions and record it in cells F1:F3.
Divide both “Lesioned area” and “Number” of lesions by the “Analyzed area mm²” in cells H5:H7 and H1:3, respectively.
Repeat steps for each section.
